q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a ball bearing?
title: Ball bearing carbon footprint per bearing
short: Weigh the rings, balls, cage and seals per bearing and multiply by the bearing steel and other suppliers' figures. Add forging or turning, heat treatment, grinding and assembly energy, then divide the plant's energy by bearings made.
audience: Bearing makers and auto component suppliers

ul: Bearing steel for rings and balls.
Rubber seals, metal shields and grease.
Hardening and tempering, often in electric or gas furnaces.

p: Report per bearing by size series and weight. Heat treatment and grinding are often the biggest energy steps, so meter them if you can.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per bearing (one month)
lines: Plant total: 172,750 / 500,000 = 0.345 kg CO2 per bearing
Add bearing steel, cage and seals for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
